standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the dimension of a fibre at a point as the sum of the dimension of the local ring of the fibre and the transcendence degree of the residue field over the residue field of the base point, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the geometric inequality to an inequality between dimensions of local rings of the two fibres.

standard_prerequisites.name: Additivity of the transcendence degree over a tower of field extensions, and the corresponding inequality and equality statements for dimensions of local rings of fibres over a base, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the field degree identity and the two local algebra statements that finish the proof.

core_obligations: Compare transcendence degrees: the residue field of the point over that of the deepest base point has degree equal to the sum of the two intermediate degrees, by additivity over the tower of extensions (proof lines 5409-5410).

Reduce to local rings: substituting this identity into the description of the fibre dimension at a point turns the claimed inequality into the corresponding inequality between the dimensions of the local rings of the two fibres (proof lines 5411-5414).

Conclude: the inequality and the equality statement under flatness both follow from the cited local algebra statements, and the flatness of the local ring of the innermost fibre over that of the fibre over the middle base follows from flatness of the local rings of the two schemes as stated by the author (proof lines 5414-5422).
proof_roadmap: Use additivity of transcendence degree and the fibre-dimension formula to reduce the claim to an inequality between local rings of fibres, then quote the algebra statements for the inequality and the flat case (proof lines 5409-5422).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a composite of locally finite type morphisms the fibre dimension at a point is at most the sum of the two relative fibre dimensions, with equality when the local ring of the innermost fibre is flat over the local ring of the fibre over the middle base (statement lines 5395-5407). The counted proof is short and complete: it applies additivity of transcendence degree over the tower of residue field extensions, uses the description of the fibre dimension at a point to rewrite the claim as an inequality between local rings of the two fibres, and concludes both the inequality and the flat equality from the cited local algebra statements, noting that flatness of the ambient local rings implies the required flatness (proof lines 5409-5422). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the fibre dimension formula and the two algebra statements.
